title: Great God! Let All Our Tuneful Powers
description: Great God! Let All Our Tuneful Powers in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Ottiwell Heginbotham wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 851 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The God of the Seasons”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great God! let all our tune-ful powers A-wake and sing thy might-y name; Thy hand rolls on our cir-cling hours, The hand from which our be-ing came.

lines: Great God! let all our tuneful powers
Awake and sing thy mighty name;
Thy hand rolls on our circling hours,
The hand from which our being came.
In beauteous order speak thy praise;
And years with smiling mercy crowned,
Each changing season on our souls
And every period, as it rolls,
Showers countless blessings on our heads.
Our lives, our health, our friends, we owe
All to thy vast unbounded love;
And hope of nobler joys above.

licence: Public domain: Ottiwell Heginbotham died in 1768.
credits: Words by Ottiwell Heginbotham (1744–1768), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
